Dual-Chain Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence Framework Targets Cross-Border Cosmetics Counterfeiting

A newly proposed traceability system integrates a dual-chain consortium blockchain with artificial intelligence to combat cosmetics counterfeiting across international online trade. Reported in the International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems, the architecture addresses rising anti-counterfeiting demands driven by the continued expansion of the cross-border e-commerce market, providing a technical framework designed to verify goods across complex distribution networks.

According to the research, conventional traceability technology struggles to counter the complex and changeable counterfeiting tactics encountered in cross-border e-commerce. Traditional systems face persistent vulnerabilities, notably the ease with which recorded information can be tampered with, the formation of isolated information islands that divide participants, and an overreliance on single anti-counterfeiting measures that fail against sophisticated illicit distribution.

To resolve these vulnerabilities, the proposed system employs a blockchain distributed ledger as its core carrier, configured as a dual-chain consortium blockchain that separates a business data chain from an audit chain. Coupled with smart contracts, the network achieves automated data collection and tamper-proof storage for cosmetic items across their entire life cycle. This continuous monitoring covers vital supply chain links, including raw material procurement, manufacturing and processing, cross-border logistics, and terminal retail sales.

The architecture pairs the secure distributed data storage of blockchain with the intelligent analysis capacity of artificial intelligence, establishing a three-dimensional anti-counterfeiting structure based on complementary technologies. The researchers conclude that this integrated model can elevate cosmetics anti-counterfeiting capabilities, mitigate purchasing risks for consumers, and serve as a practical operational paradigm for deploying blockchain and artificial intelligence in cross-border e-commerce.

Subject of Research: Blockchain and artificial intelligence traceability for cross-border cosmetics anti-counterfeiting

Article Title: The Applications of Blockchain – AI Traceability in Cross-border E-Commerce Cosmetics Anti-Counterfeiting

Article References: Hsu, H.-H., & Wang, L. (2026). The Applications of Blockchain – AI Traceability in Cross-border E-Commerce Cosmetics Anti-Counterfeiting. International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44196-026-01704-2
